item.title: Spacetech startup Cosmoserve Space raises $6 Mn in seed round
item.description:
Hyderabad-based spacetech startup Cosmoserve Space has raised $6 million in a seed funding round from Japan-based Rebright Partners, Aranya Holdings, Naandi Ventures and existing investors AUM Ventures and Shakti VC. The latest round takes its total funding to over $9 million.

In September last year, the startup raised $3.17 million in an oversubscribed pre-seed round led by Alan Rutledge, with participation from AUM Ventures and Shakti VC.

The fresh capital will support the development of Base 1, technology demonstrations and two upcoming missions, Cosmoserve said in a press release.

The startup has also inaugurated Base 1, a private facility dedicated to space debris removal and satellite servicing. The facility is designed to support the development of technologies for in-orbit repairs, refuelling and the recovery of defunct satellites.

According to the company, Base 1 is the world’s sixth facility equipped with space vision effects and microgravity simulation capabilities. It brings together infrastructure for designing, building, testing and operating technologies required for satellite servicing and space debris recovery.

Cosmoserve currently sources nearly 60% of its mission components locally. It aims to increase domestic manufacturing by developing critical technologies in-house and reducing dependence on imported optics, avionics and space-grade electronics.

In July 2026, Cosmoserve flew its first payload, Mission Embrace, aboard Skyroot Aerospace’s Vikram-1 rocket. The flight hardware was developed in under four months, six months ahead of schedule. However, the robotic capture petals did not deploy as planned, providing the company with data for further development.

Founded last year by Chiranjeevi Phanindra, Cosmoserve is developing a proprietary Dual Spacecraft Architecture to make orbital servicing more cost-efficient. The approach uses two spacecraft to service multiple satellites, instead of the conventional one-to-one recovery model.

The company estimates that its approach could bring satellite servicing costs down from around $10 million to below $1 million per satellite.

Cosmoserve plans to test its robotic capture systems through microgravity flights, reflight Mission Embrace and conduct a full-scale space debris capture demonstration in 2027.

The startup is among a growing number of Indian spacetech companies working on technologies spanning launch vehicles, satellite manufacturing, space data and orbital infrastructure. Hyderabad has also emerged as a spacetech hub, supported by its aerospace and defence ecosystem, engineering talent and research infrastructure.

item.title: Daksham Growth Ventures raises Rs 125 Cr in first close of maiden consumer fund
item.description:
Daksham Growth Ventures (DGV), the growth investment platform of multi-family office and private wealth management group Daksham Capital, has raised Rs 125 crore in the first close of its maiden consumer-focused fund, DGV Fund I.

Registered as a Category II Alternative Investment Fund (AIF) with the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI), the fund has a target corpus of Rs 150 crore, along with a greenshoe option of another Rs 150 crore, taking its potential fund size to Rs 300 crore.

The first close was anchored by family offices, high-net-worth individuals (HNIs), ultra-high-net-worth individuals (UHNIs) and entrepreneurs. The fund achieved the first close shortly after receiving SEBI registration in October 2026.

Led by Shivam Diwan, Co-Founder and Managing Partner of Daksham Growth Ventures, the fund will primarily invest in pre-Series A and Series A companies across India’s consumer ecosystem.

DGV Fund I plans to invest Rs 5 crore to Rs 20 crore in businesses that have established product-market fit and sound unit economics. It will focus on companies with annual recurring revenue (ARR) of Rs 25-75 crore and the potential to scale to Rs 300-500 crore in revenue.

The fund’s investment strategy spans four segments: direct-to-consumer (D2C) brands, consumer enablers, B2B2C and supply chain businesses, and consumer-focused artificial intelligence (AI) companies.

Beyond capital, DGV plans to support its portfolio companies through governance, financial reporting, brand positioning, leadership development and distribution expansion. The fund will also provide board participation, strategic guidance and access to industry networks to help businesses strengthen their organisational capabilities.

Daksham Capital operates across family office advisory, investment solutions, global investing, legacy and succession planning, investment banking advisory and structured lending solutions. The group said its team has advised more than 600 client families and previously managed over $1 billion in assets.

Daksham Growth Ventures is the group’s dedicated growth investment platform, focusing on consumer and consumer-allied businesses with established business models and the potential to scale sustainably.

item.title: Enrission India Capital participates in Ottonomy’s Rs 40.6 Cr funding round
item.description:
AI-powered autonomous delivery robot developer Ottonomy has raised approximately Rs 40.6 crore ($4.2 million) in a post-seed funding round, with Japan-based venture capital firm Enrission India Capital participating in the investment.

The fresh capital will support the company’s global expansion across healthcare and industrial automation, where demand for autonomous logistics solutions is increasing amid workforce shortages, Ottonomy said in a press release.

Founded by Ritukar Vijay, Ottonomy develops AI-powered autonomous delivery robots designed to operate across indoor and outdoor environments. Its flagship product, Ottobot, uses the company’s proprietary Contextual AI technology to enable autonomous deliveries across complex facilities with minimal human intervention.

The company’s robots are designed to help hospitals and enterprises automate the transportation of medicines, medical equipment, supplies and other materials. In healthcare facilities, this could help reduce the time medical professionals spend on logistical tasks and allow them to focus more on patient care.

With the latest investment, Ottonomy plans to strengthen its presence in global markets and expand the deployment of its autonomous delivery solutions across healthcare and industrial facilities.

Enrission India Capital is a Japan-based venture capital firm that invests in early-stage Indian startups, primarily from Seed to Series B. The firm focuses on sectors such as consumer, logistics, climate-tech and enterprise technology. It also works with its portfolio companies to explore international expansion opportunities, particularly in Japan. Its portfolio includes GoDesi, Pico Xpress, Uravu Labs, StackBox and Hexalog.

Ottonomy operates in the autonomous delivery and robotics segment, where companies are developing AI-powered solutions to address last-mile logistics, workforce shortages and operational efficiency across commercial and institutional settings.

In India, autonomous delivery robotics is an emerging segment, with startups exploring applications in last-mile logistics, intra-campus transportation and material movement across healthcare, manufacturing, retail and warehousing.

Other players in the broader autonomous delivery and logistics ecosystem include Airbound, which raised $37 million in a Series A round in August 2026 to scale its autonomous delivery drone technology, and Ati Motors, which raised $20 million in a Series B round in January 2025 to expand its AI-powered autonomous mobile robots for industrial material movement.

Meanwhile, Anscer Robotics raised approximately Rs 45 crore in a Series A round in 2026 to scale its autonomous mobile robots and warehouse automation solutions.

item.title: Peppermint Robotics raises Rs 100 Cr in Pre-Series B led by pi Ventures, Crane Venture Partners
item.description:
Pune-based robotics startup Peppermint Robotics has raised Rs 100 crore (around $10.5 million) in a Pre-Series B funding round led by pi Ventures and Crane Venture Partners. The round also saw participation from Asiana Fund.

The investment comprises a combination of primary capital and secondary share transactions.

The fresh capital will be used to expand manufacturing capacity, develop next-generation robotics solutions and strengthen the company's global operations. Peppermint also plans to establish an assembly line in North America in the coming months.

Founded in 2019, Peppermint Robotics develops autonomous robots for commercial floor cleaning and material transportation. The company has expanded its operations to nine countries, with the US emerging as its largest market.

Peppermint's robots are deployed across factories, hospitals, airports, malls, warehouses, hotels and universities. The company also serves pharmaceutical cleanrooms, where its robots have passed qualification testing in an EU GMP Grade cleanroom.

The startup develops its robotics hardware, software and perception systems in-house. Its robots use computer vision and LiDAR to map environments, plan cleaning routes and avoid obstacles. The company also offers offline robots for security-sensitive environments.

Peppermint plans to use the primary capital across five areas, including research and engineering, manufacturing expansion, North American operations, global market expansion and hiring senior leadership and engineering talent.

The company will also expand its portfolio of autonomous floor-cleaning and material-handling robots, while advancing its next-generation cleanroom robotics line.

Peppermint previously raised Rs 34 crore (around $4 million) in a Series A round in April 2025. According to the company, its revenue grew nearly sixfold between FY24 and FY26, after doubling last year.

item.title: Exclusive: Armatrix kicks off Rs 67 Cr seed round at 4.8X valuation premium
item.description:
Deeptech robotics startup Armatrix has raised Rs 67.28 crore in a seed funding round led by UK-based Crane Venture Partners, along with participation from new and existing investors.

The fresh funding comes less than a year after its pre-seed round and values the company nearly 5X higher than its previous round.

In January 2026, Armatrix had raised $2.1 million in a pre-seed round led by pi Ventures, with participation from Inuka Capital, Boundless Ventures, Boost VC, Turbostart and gradCapital.

According to regulatory filings accessed by Entrackr, the company has allotted 4,070 compulsory convertible preference shares (CCPS) at an issue price of Rs 1,64,900 per share, along with 10 equity shares, to raise the capital.

The funding round appears to be ongoing, with the Delhi-based company likely to raise more capital in subsequent tranches.

Crane Venture Partners led the round with an investment of Rs 40 crore. Existing investor pi Ventures infused Rs 15 crore, followed by gradCapital with Rs 4.52 crore, Boundless Ventures with Rs 2.5 crore and Inuka Capital with Rs 2.37 crore. NKSquared also joined the round with an investment of Rs 2.37 crore, marking its entry into the company.

Among other investors, AL Trust, Saurabh Chandra, Unacademy co-founder Roman Saini and existing investor Narayan Rangarajan collectively invested Rs 67 lakh in the round.

According to Entrackr's estimates, Armatrix's valuation jumped 4.8X to Rs 360 crore in the seed round from Rs 75 crore in its pre-seed round. The company plans to use the fresh proceeds for business expansion and general corporate purposes.

Founded in 2024 by Vishrant Dave, Prateesh Awasthi and Ayush Ranjan, Bengaluru-based Armatrix develops snake-like robotic manipulators for operations in hazardous and confined industrial spaces. Its technology is designed for inspection and maintenance across sectors such as shipbuilding, nuclear energy, oil and gas, and aviation, reducing the need for human workers to enter dangerous spaces.

According to Moneycontrol, Armatrix was in talks to raise $15 million in a seed round led by Crane Venture Partners.

The company remained at the pre-revenue stage in FY26 and reported a net loss of Rs 3.05 crore.

item.title: Blue Tokai crosses Rs 500 Cr revenue in FY26; losses up 54%
item.description:
Coffee chain Blue Tokai continued to expand its business in FY26, with revenue crossing the Rs 500 crore mark, supported by its presence in the organised cafe market. However, the expansion came with a higher cost burden, as losses widened 53.7% during the fiscal year ended March 2026.

Blue Tokai’s revenue from operations surged 59.4% to Rs 518 crore in FY26, compared with Rs 325 crore in FY25, according to the company’s consolidated financial statements reviewed by Entrackr.


The company also reported Rs 7.5 crore in other income, pushing its total income to Rs 525.5 crore during the last fiscal year.

Sales of coffee and related products remained Blue Tokai’s primary source of operating revenue, rising 59.3% to Rs 513 crore in FY26 from Rs 322 crore in FY25. Lease income increased 36.2% to Rs 3.5 crore, while revenue from services stood at Rs 1 crore during the fiscal year.

The increase in operating costs outpaced revenue growth, putting pressure on Blue Tokai’s profitability. The cost of materials consumed, its largest cost component, increased 65.5% to Rs 187 crore in FY26 from Rs 113 crore in FY25. Employee benefit expenses rose 35.9% to Rs 130.5 crore, while rent expenses grew 59.6% to Rs 26.65 crore during the last fiscal year.

Depreciation costs nearly 2X jumped to Rs 87 crore. Finance costs also jumped 68.8% to Rs 27 crore from Rs 16 crore in the same period.

Other expenses grew 70.5% to Rs 150 crore in FY26 from Rs 88 crore in FY25, accounting for 25% of the total expenditure. Consequently, the Gurugram-based company's total expenses increased 61.7% to Rs 608 crore in FY26 from Rs 376 crore in the previous fiscal year.

On the profitability front, Blue Tokai's EBITDA stood at Rs 23 crore in FY26, compared with Rs 19.4 crore in FY25. However, its EBITDA margin declined to 4.44% from 5.97%. The company's net losses widened 53.7% to Rs 83 crore in FY26 from Rs 54 crore in the previous fiscal year.

Blue Tokai's return on capital employed (ROCE) stood -11.94% in FY26. On a unit level, the firm spent Rs 1.17 to  earn a rupee in the same period.

The company's cash and bank balances declined to Rs 39 crore in the last fiscal year from Rs 118 crore in FY25. Meanwhile, its total assets increased to Rs 697 crore from Rs 521 crore previous fiscal year.

Blue Tokai operates in an increasingly competitive coffee market, with Third Wave Coffee among its main rivals. Third Wave is yet to disclose its FY26 financial results, while Tata Starbucks reported operating revenue of Rs 1,367 crore and a 27% reduction in net losses during the year. 

The comparison highlights the gap in scale as Blue Tokai seeks to strengthen its position in India’s organised cafe market. Its next phase will depend on growing its store network while improving store-level economics, customer retention and op-efficiency. Building scale without adding proportionate costs will remain central to its path to profitability.

item.title: Funding and acquisitions in Indian startups this week [Nov 02- Nov 07]
item.description:
This week, 28 Indian startups raised $258.1 million across three growth-stage deals and 17 early-stage deals, including two undisclosed rounds. The week also saw nine key appointments and one departure, two fund launches, an ESOP buyback and an acquisition.

In contrast, 28 startups had collectively secured about $115 million in the previous week.

[Growth-stage deals]

Growth-stage startups raised $190.5 million across three deals this week. Jewellery brand GIVA led the pack with a $100 million funding round led by Multiples Alternate Asset Management. Bengaluru-based consumer AI and entertainment company EloElo Group followed with an $80 million Series C round led by Hornbill Capital and NBCUniversal.

Pune-based robotics startup Peppermint Robotics raised Rs 100 crore (around $10.5 million) in a Pre-Series B round led by pi Ventures and Crane Venture Partners.

[Early-stage deals]

Early-stage startups raised $67.6 million across 17 deals this week. Pune-based health-tech startup Clinics On Cloud led with a $12.5 million Series A round from Dubai-based investors through Model42, powered by Enlightened Minds Investments. Bengaluru-based specialty chemicals startup altM followed with a $10.3 million Series A round led by Rainmatter by Zerodha and Mela Ventures.

AI-powered clean energy platform Two Point O Capital (TW\.O) raised $10 million in a round led by Transition Venture Capital, while wealthtech platform PowerUp Money secured $10 million led by Flourish Ventures, with participation from existing investors including Peak XV Partners, Accel and Blume Ventures.

Other startups that raised funding this week included spacetech startup Cosmoserve Space, defence technology company Axial Aero, AI-powered autonomous delivery robot developer Ottonomy, biotechnology companyVenomics AI , QSR startup The Croffle Guys and others. 

[City and segment-wise deals]

Bengaluru led startup funding activity with 6 deals during the week, followed by Delhi-NCR and Mumbai with five deals each. Pune, Hyderabad, and Gandhinagar also recorded funding this week.

E-commerce and AI startups led sector-wise funding activity with three deals each, followed by healthtech, manufacturing, fintech, foodtech and gaming, with two deals each. Robotics, spacetech and deeptech startups also secured funding during the week.

[Series-wise deals]

Seed rounds led funding activity with eight deals, followed by Series A and pre-seed rounds with four and three deals, respectively. Series C, pre-Series B, pre-Series A and angel rounds also saw activity during the week.

[Week-on-week funding trend]

On a weekly basis, startup funding more than doubled to $258.1 million from $115 million raised in the previous week.

The average weekly funding over the past eight weeks stood at around $198 million across 23 deals.

[Key Hirings]

Logistics company Porter has appointed Gaurav Jain as its chief financial officer (CFO), while Shubham Gupta and Mohit Rathi have been elevated to chief technology officer (CTO) and chief marketing officer (CMO), respectively.

Enterprise AI and analytics firm MathCo appointed Vijay Raj to its advisory board. Avendus named Sumit Agarwal as managing director and head of equity corporate finance, while Fulcrum Digital appointed Latha Nathan as senior vice president of India delivery operations. UiPath also named Yashdeep Vaishnav as its India country manager. Avendus appointed Sumit Agarwal as Managing Director and Head of Equity Corporate Finance. 

Fireside Ventures co-founder and partner Vinay Singh will exit the firm after nearly a decade, as he plans to explore opportunities in agentic commerce.

[Fund launches]

Daksham Growth Ventures (DGV), the growth investment platform of multi-family office and private wealth management group Daksham Capital, has raised Rs 125 crore in the first close of its maiden consumer-focused fund, DGV Fund I.

Private equity fund ValueQuest Tristar Fund, which backs India's advanced manufacturing sector across aerospace, defence, precision engineering and energy transition, has secured over Rs 2,100 crore in investor commitments within 15 months of its first close, surpassing its target and full greenshoe.

[Mergers & Acquisition]

Pronto founder Anjali Sardana’s physical AI venture Provision Labs has acquired Mumbai-based hardware startup Basilisk Industries for an undisclosed sum, with Basilisk founder Shourya Watwani set to lead Provision’s hardware efforts and develop its in-house post-processing models.

[ESOP Buyback]

Talent mobility platform Leverage Edu has launched its third ESOP buyback programme and granted stock options to 100 more employees, taking the share of its workforce with equity in the company to 23%. The programme allows employees to cash out a portion of their vested options. The company previously conducted buybacks in June 2022 and June 2024.

[Financial results this week]

[New launches and partnerships]

▪️ Cashfree launches Checkout for Agents, enabling AI agents to complete payments seamlessly at checkout

Cashfree, an AI-native payments platform, has launched Checkout for Agents, becoming the first Indian payments company to integrate the WebMCP standard into its checkout. The feature enables AI agents to complete transactions on behalf of consumers and is available across Cashfree’s hosted checkout, payment forms and payment links without requiring merchants to change their existing integrations. WebMCP allows AI agents to interact with websites through a defined set of actions instead of decoding page layouts and underlying code, potentially reducing token consumption during checkout by over 40%.

▪️ super.money expands financial offerings with digital gold, offers 3% assured cashback on purchases ahead of Dhanteras

super.money, a fintech platform focused on Gen Z consumers, has launched 24-karat digital gold on its app ahead of Dhanteras, expanding beyond its UPI-led payments business. Customers can buy gold starting at Rs 10 and receive assured 3% cashback on every purchase. Sourced and stored through SafeGold, the offering allows users to buy and sell gold through UPI without making or storage charges. Cashback is capped at Rs 9,000 per user per month, with a purchase limit of Rs 50,000.

▪️ InMobi, BMRCL sign MoU to promote sustainable urban mobility at Ibbaluru Metro Station

InMobi has signed a 30-year agreement with Bangalore Metro Rail Corporation Limited (BMRCL) to secure naming rights for Ibbaluru Metro Station in Bengaluru. Under the agreement, the company will pay Rs 65 crore, excluding GST, and the station will be renamed InMobi Ibbaluru Metro Station.

▪️ Procol to launch Clara 2.0 multi-agent source-to-pay platform at Gartner IT Symposium Kochi

SProcol's Clara 2.0 features specialised AI agents for procurement and finance, automating workflows across purchasing, sourcing, supplier risk monitoring, spend management and invoice processing. The platform integrates with existing ERP systems through two-way data synchronisation and has helped reduce procurement cycle times by up to 80% across Procol's customer base.

[News flash this week]

▪️ Scripbox to convert into public company ahead of IPO plans

Bengaluru-based wealthtech startup Scripbox has approved its conversion into a public limited company, signalling preparations for a potential IPO. According to regulatory filings accessed by Entrackr, the board has approved changing its name from Scripbox Wealth Managers Private Limited to Scripbox Wealth Managers Limited. The proposed IPO will comprise a fresh issue of equity shares and an offer for sale (OFS) by existing shareholders.

▪️ Razorpay receives SEBI approval for IPO

Fintech unicorn Razorpay has received SEBI approval for its proposed IPO, according to sources. The Bengaluru-based company had confidentially filed its DRHP in June 2026 and is targeting to raise Rs 5,500-6,500 crore at an expected valuation of $5 billion (Rs 49,000-50,000 crore). It is expected to file its final IPO papers before March 2027.

▪️ TVS retains EV two-wheeler lead in October; Ather grows 3%, Ola declines 10%

India’s electric two-wheeler market recorded 2,23,847 registrations in October, up from 2,08,705 units in September, according to Vahan data. TVS Motor retained the top spot with 60,429 registrations and a 27% market share, followed by Bajaj Auto with 49,067 units and a 21.92% share.

Ather Energy ranked third with 31,796 registrations, up 2.75% month-on-month, while Hero MotoCorp recorded 29,901 units, a 22.34% increase. Ola Electric remained fifth with 12,096 registrations, down 10.12% from September, making it the only player among the top five to report a monthly decline.

▪️ UPI hits record 25.47 billion transactions in October, daily value crosses Rs 1 lakh crore

UPI processed a record 25.47 billion transactions worth Rs 31.53 lakh crore in October 2026, according to NPCI data. Transaction volume rose 5.8% month-on-month from 24.07 billion in September, while transaction value increased 7.4% from Rs 29.37 lakh crore. On a year-on-year basis, volume grew 23% and value increased 16%. On a daily basis, UPI averaged 822 million transactions worth Rs 1.02 lakh crore in October, compared to 802 million transactions worth Rs 97,913 crore in September.

▪️Angel One overtakes Zerodha to become second-largest broker; Groww adds over 3 lakh clients in October

Angel One overtook Zerodha to become India’s second-largest stock broker in October 2026, adding nearly 2.43 lakh active clients during the month. Meanwhile, Groww maintained its leadership position with over 1.37 crore active clients, while discount broking platform Sahi recorded the fastest monthly growth among the top 20 brokers.
